sourceRestrictions: Assess only Matt Dillahunty and Randal Rauser in their opening speeches and direct debate, including the concluding exchange, approximately 0:22–1:09:31. Exclude every enumerated host/logistics interval and all audience Q&A, dependent answers, post-Q&A exchange, thanks and promotional material. No credit, penalty, reply link or absence inference may come from excluded material. No paired formal closing speeches occur.

The motion compares which framework is better for society and promotes human flourishing in this life. Both speakers set aside proving whether Christianity or humanism is ultimately true. Do not convert the motion to proving God, Christianity, atheism, or the resurrection. Assess demands for public justification and practical grounding as actually argued; do not declare stipulated premises established facts.

Dillahunty grants historical Christian benefits and says humanism can adopt beneficial practices from other sources. His claim is revisability, equal human worth, cooperation, and publicly assessable consequences. He concedes that humanists can violate their own principles. His equal-voting argument distinguishes a categorical sex exclusion from individual restrictions or abolishing voting for everyone; retain this qualification.

Rauser defends mere Christianity associated with the Apostles Creed and emulating Jesus; he is egalitarian, acknowledges Christian failures and shared humanist values, and rejects treating American dispensationalism as all Christianity. Preserve his intrinsic image-of-God account, the difference between rights existing and being codified, his point that neither framework has proved its premises, and his fallibilist rather than infallible treatment of moral intuitions.

The abandoned infant/anencephaly case concerns worth without self-valuation or others valuing the person. Do not turn Matt’s assisted-dying aside into endorsement of killing an infant, or attribute involuntary euthanasia to either speaker. The chimpanzee/fire case is an intuition/coherence challenge with a consequentialist qualification, not an independently conducted experiment.

Automatic captions sometimes corrupt names and terms (Dillahunty, Carl Sagan, Mary Warnock, imago Dei, anencephalic, complementarian, noetic, ratiocination).
